problem: Whitening is written as Z = Σ^(−1/2)(X − μ) with no condition on Σ. If Σ is singular (the case Section 1 itself allows), no inverse square root exists and Z cannot have identity covariance with independent standard normal components.
fix: Add: 'When Σ is invertible, let Σ^(−1/2) be the inverse of a symmetric square root of Σ and set Z = Σ^(−1/2)(X − μ); then E[Z] = 0 and Cov(Z) = I, so the components of Z are independent standard normals. If Σ is singular, only the non-degenerate directions can be whitened, and the rest collapse to constants.'

problem: It says the joint density of two uncorrelated components factors into the product of marginals, but Section 1 already stated that no density exists in ℝⁿ when Σ is singular. The two statements contradict each other in the singular case.
fix: Write: 'If two components of a multivariate normal vector are uncorrelated, they are independent — when Σ is invertible their joint density factors into the product of the two marginals, and in general the characteristic function factors in the same way.'

problem: The trap says only that 'a negative determinant is impossible'. This can mislead a student into thinking any symmetric matrix with a non-negative determinant is a valid covariance matrix, which is false (e.g. [[1, 2], [2, 1]] is indefinite, and other 3×3 cases fail even with positive determinant).
fix: Write: 'Forgetting that Σ must be symmetric and positive semidefinite; a negative determinant, or a negative diagonal entry, is impossible, and every principal submatrix must also have a non-negative determinant.'
